Synesthesia is a rare perceptual condition causing unusual sensations, which are triggered by the stimulation of otherwise unrelated modalities (e.g., the sensation of colors triggered when listening to music).

The first term was provided by the French physician Charles-Auguste-Édouard Cornaz (1825–1911) in his medical dissertation about eye diseases; he named it hyperchromatopsie ( perception de trop de couleurs ) (hyperchromatopsia [perception of too many colors]; Cornaz 1848 , 150; cf. Jewanski et al. 2012 ).
He named it, therefore, pseudochromesthésie (pseudochromesthesia), because of the perception of false colors (Chabalier 1864 ).
He used it specifically for phenomena linking touch or light to coughing or sneezing (see below), which he related to the tail of the medulla oblongata (in the brainstem) in particular.
